findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: The person in charge (PIC) could not show proof of his food manager certificate. Ensure that every person that handles food and clean dishes obtains a food manager certificate and be sure that certificates are made available for all routine inspections.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Required records available: molluscan shellfish identification, and parasite destruction.
findings.comment: The facility could not produce a letter of guarantee form for their sushi supplier. Discussed with the PIC that the purpose of the form is to certify that the raw fish supplier complies with food safety laws and has followed the proper procedures to remove parasites. Ensure that letter of guarantee forms are current per calendar year and are available for routine inspections. Will follow-up September 2, 2026 to see that form is available.
findings.citation_text: 3-402.11(A) Parasite Destruction. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, before service or sale in READY TO-EAT form, raw, raw-marinated, partially cooked, or marinated-partially cooked FISH shall be: (1) Frozen and stored at a temperature of -20°C (-4°F) or below for a minimum of 168 hours (7 days) in a freezer; (2) Frozen at -35°C (-31°F) or below until solid and stored at -35°C (-31°F) or below for a minimum of 15 hours; or (3) Frozen at -35°C (-31°F) or below until solid and stored at -20°C (-4°F) or below for a minimum of 24 hours.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment:
There has been a history of falsifying pH logs for the acidified sushi rice. See violation #29 for further details. The PIC has continuously falsified data logged within record logs.This violation alone will warrant a number of additional spot checks to ensure staff is properly trained and understands the importance of monitoring and logging. 

PIC has not demonstrated knowledge of food safety practices. PIC has continued to operate without essential equipment (pH meter) or other interim measures in place. Operator was noted to have falsified data logged within record logs. This violation alone will warrant a number of additional spot checks to insure staff is properly trained and understands the importance of monitoring and logging. See violations below.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(A) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection. [Pf]

findings.title: Compliance with variance/specialized process/HACCP.
findings.comment:
It is evident that the PIC is falsifying pH records. The PIC noted two pH recordings, however, one of the recordings had been pre written for a future time (9:59am). Discussed with the PIC that falsifying records is against the facility’s HACCP Plan and also inaccurate record keeping. Ensure that pH records are accurate and never falsified. Will follow-up on April 6, 2026 to ensure that records are being correctly monitored by the PIC. 

Logs and discussion with the PIC indicate sushi rice pH and pH meter logs have been falsified. Logs reflect that the pH meter has been calibrated and sushi pH measured over the last week despite the lack of a functional pH meter in the facility. Staff must record accurate HACCP records. Inspector will follow up to see that accurate logs are maintained.
findings.citation_text: 8-103.12(C) Conformance with Approved Procedures. If the REGULATORY AUTHORITY grants a VARIANCE as specified in § 8-103.10, or a HACCP PLAN is otherwise required as specified under § 8-201.13, the PERMIT HOLDER shall: (C) Maintain and provide to the regulatory authority, upon request, records specified under § 8-201.14 (D) and (E)(3) that demonstrate that the following are routinely employed; (1) Procedures for monitoring the CRITICAL CONTROL POINTS, (2) Monitoring of the CRITICAL CONTROL POINTS, (3) Verification of the effectiveness of the operation or process, and (4) Necessary corrective actions if there is failure at a CRITICAL CONTROL POINT.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
findings.comment: Sushi rice is not acidified, nor is a Time as a Control policy in place to maintain food safety while rice is held on the countertop to make sushi rolls. Discussed the use of Time as a Control with PIC. If sushi rice used from cooking, rolls created from that rice need to be created and sold within 4 hours of rice being removed from the rice cooker. If sushi rice is cooled to 41F within 6 hours (and logs are maintained), sushi rolls created from that rice need to be sold within 6 hours of the rice being removed from cold-holding. Sushi packages need to be labeled to indicate the time that they should be consumed by.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from temperature control. [Pf]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
PIC was observed touching face and other surfaces before donning gloves to engage in food preparation. Hand washing did not occur before between activities. The activity was ceased and PIC was instructed to wash hands before putting on a fresh pair of gloves. Ensure that hand washing occurs before donning gloves if task changes. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed several TCS foods stored in the reach-in cooler to not be date marked. These items include but are not limited to imitation crab, chicken, shrimp, and homemade sauce. Discussed with PIC that items should be date marked if stored in house for longer than 24 hours. Ensure that TCS food is date marked if stored in house longer than 24 hours and discarded if not used within 7 days. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
An employee was observed turning off faucet handles using barehands during the hand-washing process. Discussed with PIC that employees must use a barrier when turning off the faucet to prevent recontaminating hands and to also educated employees. Ensure that employees always use a barrier when turning off faucet handles after the hand-washing process. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 (B) Sauce was observed without a date mark in the reach-in section of the prep cooler. PIC stated sauce was made 2 days ago. Label with proper date mark was provided during inspection. Ensure proper date marking for ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety foods and all products that will not be used within 24hrs as required by company HACCP plan.
A Refrigerated, ready to eat, TCS food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41F/below for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp wiping cloth was folded and stored on the top edge of the sani-bucket. Proper storage in sanitizer solution between uses was discussed. Wiping cloth was placed in the solution to allow for proper storage.
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Employees were not following requirements of the company HACCP plan. Sushi products prepared prior to inspector’s arrival were observed with internal temperatures above 50F in the display cooler, indicting they were not properly chilled to 41F/below prior to placement in the cooler. PIC confirmed products were placed directly in the display cooler after preparation. Sushi is to be chilled properly in the walk-in cooler or freezer prior to placing items in the display cooler or transporting to other stores. 
Sushi products prepared within the last 2hrs were sitting at room temperature in the prep area, and a California roll had an internal temperature of 64F. Sushi products should be placed in the walk-in cooler or freezer as soon as possible after preparation to ensure proper chilling and limit time in the temperature danger zone. 
Daily logs sheets for previous operating days show documentation, but PIC noted information for the current operating day was not yet written down. The pH meter is to be calibrated each day prior to use, and the pH of sushi rice should be checked prior to use to confirm a pH of 4.1 or below. Food handler stated sushi rice had a pH of 3.9 when checked this morning. Employees were advised to write down information as they go to ensure proper documentation.
Thermometer available for use has a probe to take internal temperatures and also has the ability to take surface temperatures via an infrared option. PIC stated they use the infrared option for temperature documentation. The thermometer has not been calibrated recently to ensure accuracy. Per HACCP information the thermometer should be checked at minimum weekly. PIC was advised to use the ice point method to calibrate the probe thermometer (32F) and use the probe thermometer to verify internal temperatures of foods during daily temperature checks. 
Facility is currently without a certified food manager, as both the PIC and other employee have expired certifications. 
Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at a follow-up inspection in 2 weeks.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Food manager certifications are expired for staff working at the facility. PIC has a certification that expired as of December 2022, and the other employee has a certification that expired in May of 2022. PIC was advised on the need for re-certification as soon as possible to ensure a certified food manager is present during all hours of operation.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Prepared sushi products in the display cooler had internal temperatures at 51F-54F for a California roll, spicy roll, and chef’s choice. PIC stated products were prepared this morning and placed directly in the display cooler. Products are to be properly chilled to 41F/below prior to placing items in the display cooler. Products were taken to walk-in freezer to quickly chill to 41F.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Prepared sushi products made within the last 2hrs were sitting in the prep area. The internal temperature of a California roll was observed at 64F. PIC was advised on best practices to limit the time prepared products sit at room temperature to avoid temperature abuse. Products need to be placed in the walk-in freezer or walk-in cooler after preparation to chill to 41F/below and be maintained at proper temperature until items are placed in the display cooler or transported to other locations for service. All products were placed in the walk-in freezer to quickly chill sushi to 41F.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 (B) Portions of cream cheese and imitation crab meat were observed without date marks in the walk-in cooler. PIC noted all products are typically used within 3 days. PIC was advised the company’s HACCP plan requires dating of all foods that will not be used within 24hrs. Ensure proper date marking for ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety foods and all products that will not be used within 24hrs as required by company HACCP plan.
Except as specified in  (E) -(G) of this section, refrigerated, ready to eat TCS food prepared and packaged by a food processing plant shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in  (A). The day the original container is opened in the food establishment shall be counted as Day 1, and the day or date marked by the food establishment may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Tempura shrimp was observed with an internal temperature of 63F-68F in pan sitting at room temperature on top of the prep cooler. PIC confirmed the shrimp was fried around 7am and was sitting out at room temperature to cool prior to use. Shrimp was used to prepare sushi products starting around 8:30am. Shrimp was taken to walk-in cooler to chill until it was needed again to prepare products.
Best practices were discussed for cooling and cold holding cooked tempura shrimp. Shrimp should not sit at room temperature for hours while cooling and during preparation of sushi products. Ensure shrimp is placed in the walk-in cooler or walk-in freezer in a loosely covered or uncovered pan protected from cross contamination to allow for quick chilling. Remove shrimp from cold holding when it is time to prepare sushi containing tempura shrimp, and place shrimp in the cooler when not in use. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp wiping cloth was observed on the prep table next to the rice cooker. Proper storage of wiping cloths in sanitizer solution between uses was discussed. Wiping cloth was taken to soiled linen storage. Ensure wiping cloths are stored properly between uses. 
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Wet wiping cloths were observed not stored in sanitizer solution. Ensure wet wiping cloths are stored in sanitizer solution. Wiping cloth moved into sani bucket during the inspection. 
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: 4-303.11: Observed no sani buckets being used during the inspection. Sani buckets were made during the inspection to correct the violation. (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-301.11: Observed a small bowl being used as a scoop inside a container of food in the prep cooler. All scoops must have a handle to avoid contamination of food from hands. The bowl was replaced with a scoop with a handle. 
(A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall properly wash hands (C). (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands – except washing fruits and veggies (P). (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize contact with FOOD that is not RTE (Pf). (D) Contact does not apply to RTE Food being added as ingredient to be cooked. (E) FOOD EMPLOYEES not serving a HSP may contact exposed, RTE with bare hands if approved.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-201.11: Observed the quat sani bucket to be stored on top of the prep table. The sani bucket must be stored below food and food contact surfaces to avoid contamination of food and food contact surfaces. The sani bucket was moved during the inspection. 

(A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).
